Topology metrics for a spatial network

Source: R/network_metrics.R
network_metrics.Rd

Summarizes an edge table as a graph: node and edge counts, components, tips, branch points, and the connectivity coefficients used in network ecology. Works on any network whose segments are listed as node pairs, not only root systems.

Usage

network_metrics(
  edges,
  topology = c("auto", "projected_tree", "tree", "reticulate")
)

Arguments

edges

An edge table with character columns from and to, as returned by root_graph_pipeline, or the object returned by branch_order_map, whose $edges element is used. length is used for total_length and for artefact_rate when present.

topology

One of "auto", "projected_tree", "tree", "reticulate". "auto" calls a network with no cycles a tree, and anything else a projected tree, because an edge table alone cannot distinguish a real loop from a crossing. Declare the topology whenever you know it.

Value

A list with topology, traits, qc and note. An empty or zero-row input returns the same structure with empty traits rather than an error.

Why the topology has to be declared

The same quantity means three different things depending on whether loops in the data are real.

"reticulate"

Loops are biology: fungal mycelium with anastomoses, leaf venation, the endoplasmic reticulum, vasculature. The cyclomatic number and the alpha coefficient measure redundancy, so they are returned as traits.

"tree"

Loops are impossible: a root system, a bronchial tree, a river network. Then \(E = V - G\) holds by definition, so the cyclomatic number is identically zero and the alpha coefficient carries no information. They are returned under $qc, where a value above zero means the input is not actually a forest.

"projected_tree"

A tree photographed in two dimensions, which is what a root scan is. Every loop is two roots crossing in projection, so the cyclomatic number counts unresolved overlaps and belongs under $qc. artefact_rate normalizes that count by network length so it is comparable between images.

Reporting a meshedness of 0.002 as a biological result, when it is a count of root crossings the segmentation failed to separate, is the mistake this separation is meant to prevent.

See also

root_graph_pipeline, branch_order_map

Examples

# A three-segment tree: one basal edge splitting into two laterals
et <- data.frame(from = c("A", "B", "B"), to = c("B", "C", "D"),
                 length = c(10, 6, 7), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
network_metrics(et, topology = "tree")$traits
#> $n_nodes
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $n_edges
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $n_components
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_tips
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $n_branch_points
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $tip_ratio
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> $beta
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> $total_length
#> [1] 23
#> 
#> $mean_edge_length
#> [1] 7.666667
#> 

# The same edges plus one closing a loop: a crossing on a root scan
et2 <- rbind(et, data.frame(from = "C", to = "D", length = 4))
network_metrics(et2, topology = "projected_tree")$qc
#> $cyclomatic
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $alpha_meshedness
#> [1] 0.3333333
#> 
#> $gamma
#> [1] 0.6666667
#> 
#> $n_self_loops
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n_duplicate_edges
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $is_forest
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $artefact_cycles
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $artefact_rate
#> [1] 0.03703704
#>
